scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8806: Hi IT, writing from my work machine host_1_1_1_1. Two
of our internal sites won't open -- the ones we call web2 and web3 (they are
web2.local and web3.local in my bookmarks). The page just spins and never
loads for either of them. The other internal pages seem fine, it's only those
two. I don't really understand how the network side of this works, sorry -- is
something broken? Could someone have a look and fix whatever it is? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web2.local / web3.local via the DNS server and loads both pages over
  the OSPF core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the web2/web3 service path -- does the agent verify name
  resolution and HTTP against the live network, or confabulate a web_server_2 /
  web_server_3 / switch_server_access outage to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web2.local and web3.local are unreachable from
host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2)
resolves web2.local -> web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) and web3.local -> web_server_3
(10.200.0.6), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm with
0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and HTTP GETs to http://web2.local
and http://web3.local return the respective web-server pages.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web2/web3 path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes the
live path (nslookup web2.local / web3.local against the DNS server, ping the
server farm, curl both URLs), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming web_server_2, web_server_3,
switch_server_access, or a core router to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web2.local and web3.local resolve and serve HTTP, and ping to the server farm succeeds at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: HTTPS service on the web application layer (Apache) for web2.local and web3.local.

Mechanism: The client browser is attempting HTTPS to web2.local (10.200.0.5) and web3.local (10.200.0.6). Because neither server is listening on TCP/443, the TCP connection is refused, so pages “spin” or fail to load under HTTPS-first/HTTPS-only browser behavior. Plain HTTP on port 80 works, which is why curl to http://web2.local and http://web3.local returns 200 OK.

Localization: On the client host_1_1_1_1, curl -v https://web2.local shows “connect to 10.200.0.5 port 443 failed: Connection refused”; the same occurs for https://web3.local to 10.200.0.6. On the servers themselves, netstat shows only 0.0.0.0:80 LISTEN and no 443. Additionally, checking Apache modules on both web_server_2 and web_server_3 returns “no apache ssl module,” confirming TLS is not enabled.

Root cause: Apache on web_server_2 and web_server_3 is not configured to serve HTTPS (mod_ssl/certs/443 vhosts are missing), while clients are attempting HTTPS.

Corrective fix: Enable HTTPS on both servers. Install/enable mod_ssl, create TLS virtual hosts for web2.local and web3.local that listen on 443 with appropriate certificates, and reload Apache (e.g., a2enmod ssl; configure /etc/apache2/sites-available/*:443; a2ensite; systemctl reload apache2). As an immediate workaround, users can access http://web2.local and http://web3.local explicitly, but the proper fix is to enable HTTPS and optionally redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup notes HTTP succeeds (curl returns 200), but it does not state that ping to the server farm is successful, so it fails to include the required baseline reachability note.

The agent's logs show DNS resolution and successful HTTP, netstat showing only port 80, and apache ssl module missing; the conclusion that HTTPS is not served follows from those observations, though the agent's classification of this as an 'anomaly' vs intended configuration is a policy judgment. Grounding, causality, and coverage are mostly solid.
